Surah al-'Asr is Makkan. [[Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Surah (Wal-'Asr) was revealed in Makkah. See: al-Durr al-Manthur, 8/621.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿By the 'Asr﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: By time (al-dahr). It is said: He swore by it because it holds a lesson for the one who reflects. It is also said: its meaning is "by the Lord of the 'Asr," and likewise in similar oaths. Ibn Kaysan said: By al-'Asr He meant the night and the day, which are called the two 'Asrs (al-'Asran). Al-Hasan said: It is the time from the decline of the sun until its setting. [[See: 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir, 2/394; Fath al-Bari, 8/729.]] Qatadah said: It is the last hour of the hours of the day. [[Reported by 'Abd al-Razzaq in his Tafsir, 2/394, without the word "last."]] Muqatil said: He swore by the 'Asr prayer, which is the middle prayer (al-salah al-wusta).

﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾ that is, in loss and diminishment. It is said: By this He meant [the disbeliever] [[In manuscript "B": the disbeliever.]], as proven by the fact that He made an exception of the believers. "Loss" (al-khusran) is the forfeiting of a person's capital through the destruction of his soul and his lifespan [by acts of disobedience] [[An addition from "B".]], and these two are the greatest part of his capital.

﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ for they are not in loss. ﴿and advise one another﴾ that is, they enjoin one another, ﴿to the truth﴾ meaning the Qur'an; this was said by al-Hasan and Qatadah. Muqatil said: to faith and the oneness of Allah (tawhid).

﴿and advise one another to patience﴾ in fulfilling the obligations and upholding the command of Allah. Ibn 'Awn narrated from Ibrahim who said: He meant that when a person is granted a long life in this world and grows old, he is in decline and regression, except the believers, for there is written for them their rewards and the good of their deeds which they used to do in their youth and health. This is like His saying: "We certainly created man in the best of forms; then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds."
